title: Ampleness can be checked on a closed subscheme with the same underlying space
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of Noetherian schemes (each locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; schemes as in [def-pc-scheme]) such that the underlying continuous map of $i$ is a homeomorphism of $Z$ onto $X$. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $i^*\mathcal L$ its pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] (an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module). Then $i^*\mathcal L$ is ample on $Z$ if and only if $\mathcal L$ is ample on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

proof.text: ($\mathcal L$ ample $\Rightarrow$ $i^*\mathcal L$ ample.) The closed immersion $i$ is finite, in particular affine [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. The pullback of an ample invertible module along an affine morphism is ample [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible]; so if $\mathcal L$ is ample on $X$, then $i^*\mathcal L$ is ample on $Z$. The rest of the proof shows the converse; assume from now on that $i^*\mathcal L$ is ample.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS (coherent-lemma-ample-on-reduction, coherent.tex line 4737), proof, first sentence: 'If $\mathcal L$ is ample, then $i^*\mathcal L$ is ample for example by Morphisms, Lemma 0892'

proof.text: (The ideal sheaf is nilpotent.) Let $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ be the ideal sheaf of $i$, a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; its powers $\mathcal I^k$ are the quasi-coherent ideals with $\mathcal I^k(U)=\mathcal I(U)^k$ on affine opens $U$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. The underlying set of the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal I$ is $V(\mathcal I)=\{x:\mathcal I_x\neq\mathcal O_{X,x}\}$ and equals $i(Z)$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine]; as $i$ is a homeomorphism onto $X$, $V(\mathcal I)=X$. The module $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent (on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] it is $\widetilde A$) and of finite type (the identity $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$ is a surjection from $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus1}$) [pqf-def-coherent], hence coherent since $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Its support [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] is $X$ (each stalk $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a local ring, so nonzero), which is contained in $V(\mathcal I)=X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-support-power-ideal-kills] applied to $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal K=\mathcal I$, $\mathcal I^t\mathcal O_X=0$ for some $t\ge0$. Here $\mathcal I^t\mathcal O_X$ is the image of $\mathcal I^t\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0), which is $\mathcal I^t$ itself (for $t=0$, $\mathcal O_X$). If $t=0$ then $\mathcal O_X=0$ and so $\mathcal I=0$. In every case $\mathcal I^m=0$ for all $m\ge\max(t,1)$, since $\mathcal I^m(U)=\mathcal I(U)^m\subseteq\mathcal I(U)^t=0$ on affine opens and a quasi-coherent module vanishing on an affine open cover is zero. Fix $n\ge2$ with $\mathcal I^n=0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS (coherent-lemma-ample-on-reduction, coherent.tex line 4737), proof, first paragraph: 'Since $i(Z) = X$ set theoretically we see that $\mathcal I^n = 0$ for some $n$ by Lemma 01Y9'

proof.text: (The chain of closed subschemes.) For $1\le k\le n$ let $i_k:Z_k\to X$ be a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I^k$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme]: for $k=1$ take $Z_1=Z$, $i_1=i$ (ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$); for $k=n$ take $Z_n=X$, $i_n=\mathrm{id}_X$ (a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\ker(\mathrm{id})=0=\mathcal I^n$); for $1<k<n$ any closed immersion with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I^k$. For every affine open $U\subseteq X$ with $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $I=\mathcal I(U)$, the open $i_k^{-1}(U)$ is affine and $i_k^{-1}(U)\to U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I^k)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme], [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] (for $k=1,n$ by the same node together with [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic], which identifies $Z_k$ with the closed subscheme it constructs, over $X$). For $2\le k\le n$, $\mathcal I^k\subseteq\mathcal I^{k-1}$ (on affine opens $I^k\subseteq I^{k-1}$), so there is a closed immersion $j_k:Z_{k-1}\to Z_k$ with $i_k\circ j_k=i_{k-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS (coherent-lemma-ample-on-reduction, coherent.tex line 4737), proof, first paragraph: 'Consider the sequence $X = Z_n \supset Z_{n-1} \supset \ldots \supset Z_1 = Z$ of closed subschemes cut out by $0 = \mathcal I^n \subset \mathcal I^{n-1} \subset \ldots \subset \mathcal I$'

proof.text: (Each $Z_k$ is Noetherian and each $j_k$ is a homeomorphism.) By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine], $i_k(Z_k)=V(\mathcal I^k)$, and on an affine open $U$ (notation of step 3) $V(\mathcal I^k)\cap U=V(I^k)=V(I)=V(\mathcal I)\cap U$, since a prime ideal contains $I^k$ iff it contains $I$. Hence $i_k(Z_k)=V(\mathcal I)=X$ (step 2), and $i_k$, a homeomorphism onto its closed image [def-weil-closed-immersion], is a homeomorphism $Z_k\to X$. So $Z_k$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], $X$ being so. Take an affine open covering $X=\bigcup_aU_a$ with $R_a=\mathcal O_X(U_a)$ Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; then $Z_k=\bigcup_ai_k^{-1}(U_a)$ with $i_k^{-1}(U_a)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R_a/\mathcal I(U_a)^k)$ (step 3) and $R_a/\mathcal I(U_a)^k$ Noetherian (an ascending chain of ideals of the quotient pulls back to an ascending chain of ideals of $R_a$) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; so $Z_k$ is locally Noetherian, hence Noetherian. Since $i_k\circ j_k=i_{k-1}$ with $i_k,i_{k-1}$ homeomorphisms onto $X$, $j_k=i_k^{-1}\circ i_{k-1}$ on underlying spaces is a homeomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS (coherent-lemma-ample-on-reduction, coherent.tex line 4737), proof, first paragraph: the $Z_k$ are closed subschemes of the Noetherian scheme $X$ with the same underlying space (implicit in the reduction)

proof.text: (Each $j_k$ has a square-zero ideal sheaf.) Let $2\le k\le n$ and $\mathcal J_k=\ker(\mathcal O_{Z_k}\to j_{k*}\mathcal O_{Z_{k-1}})$, the ideal sheaf of $j_k$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. The opens $V=i_k^{-1}(U)$, $U\subseteq X$ affine, are affine and cover $Z_k$, with $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R/I^k)$ and $j_k^{-1}(V)=i_{k-1}^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R/I^{k-1})$ (step 3). On global sections over these, $i_k\circ j_k=i_{k-1}$ says that the composite $R\to R/I^k\to\mathcal O_{Z_{k-1}}(j_k^{-1}V)=R/I^{k-1}$ is the quotient map; since $R\to R/I^k$ is surjective, the ring map of $j_k$ over $V$ is the canonical surjection $R/I^k\to R/I^{k-1}$, with kernel $I^{k-1}/I^k$. So $\mathcal J_k(V)=I^{k-1}/I^k$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and $\mathcal J_k(V)^2=(I^{2k-2}+I^k)/I^k=0$ because $2k-2\ge k$ for $k\ge2$. Then $\mathcal J_k^2|_V=(\mathcal J_k(V)^2)^\sim=0$ for every $V$ of this affine open cover [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], so $\mathcal J_k^2=0$ (a sheaf zero on an open cover is zero).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS (coherent-lemma-ample-on-reduction, coherent.tex line 4737), proof, first paragraph: 'Then each of the closed immersions $Z_{i-1} \to Z_i$ is defined by a coherent sheaf of ideals of square zero'

proof.text: (The pulled back modules.) For $1\le k\le n$ put $\mathcal L_k=i_k^*\mathcal L$, an invertible $\mathcal O_{Z_k}$-module [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible]. Then $\mathcal L_1=i^*\mathcal L$, $\mathcal L_n=\mathrm{id}_X^*\mathcal L\cong\mathcal L$, and for $2\le k\le n$, $j_k^*\mathcal L_k=j_k^*i_k^*\mathcal L\cong(i_k\circ j_k)^*\mathcal L=\mathcal L_{k-1}$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition], [def-pc-module-pullback]. Ampleness of an invertible module [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] depends only on its isomorphism class: an isomorphism $\varphi:\mathcal M\cong\mathcal N$ induces isomorphisms $\varphi^{\otimes m}:\mathcal M^{\otimes m}\cong\mathcal N^{\otimes m}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and, on stalks, $s_x\in\mathfrak m_x\mathcal M^{\otimes m}_x$ iff $\varphi^{\otimes m}(s)_x\in\mathfrak m_x\mathcal N^{\otimes m}_x$, so $X_s=X_{\varphi^{\otimes m}(s)}$ for every global section $s$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS (coherent-lemma-ample-on-reduction, coherent.tex line 4737), proof, first paragraph, implicit: the restrictions of $\mathcal L$ to the $Z_k$ and their compatibility along $Z_{k-1}\to Z_k$

proof.text: (Induction; conclusion.) Claim: for $1\le k\le n$, $\mathcal L_k$ is ample on $Z_k$. Base $k=1$: $\mathcal L_1=i^*\mathcal L$ is ample by assumption. Step: let $2\le k\le n$ and $\mathcal L_{k-1}$ ample. Then $j_k^*\mathcal L_k\cong\mathcal L_{k-1}$ is ample (step 6), and $j_k:Z_{k-1}\to Z_k$ is a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes (steps 3, 4) whose ideal sheaf has square zero (step 5), with $\mathcal L_k$ invertible (step 6); by [lem-sc-ample-square-zero-thickening], $\mathcal L_k$ is ample. For $k=n$: $\mathcal L_n\cong\mathcal L$ is ample, so $\mathcal L$ is ample on $X$ (step 6).
